title: Antifreeze - Ethylene Glycol vs. Propylene Glycol
description: Comparing ethylene glycol and propylene glycol antifreeze properties

rows: More antifreeze is needed of propylene glycol to achieve the same freeze point
Ethylene glycol has superior heat transfer efficiency due to lower viscosity - but more fluid must be circulated to transfer the same amount of energy since Propylene glycol has higher specific heat
Propylene glycol increases major head loss in the systems. Pumps head increased
Needs more than 20 - 30 days to degrade
A carcinogen is any substance or agent that promotes cancer
High level of acute when taken orally, targets the kidneys
Ethylene glycol should never be used in any drinking water or food processing system
Propylene glycol is used in small amounts in cosmetics
